_comment: Documented alternative conceptions for the tree-mass topic, authored by the procedure in docs/misconception_library.md. Every persona for this topic is built on the first entry; the rest are recorded because the research was done. Ordering is by how well documented the conception is, not by how interesting it is. Citations live in tree-mass.sources.md.
canonical_explanation: Most of a tree's dry mass is carbon the tree takes from carbon dioxide in the air during photosynthesis; the soil supplies only a small fraction of minerals.

misconceptions.name: A tree's mass comes from the soil
misconceptions.belief: The tree gets big by pulling stuff up out of the dirt through its roots. That is what roots are for, and that is why you plant a tree in good soil and feed it.
misconceptions.predicts: Weigh the pot of soil when the seed goes in and again twenty years later and it would be much lighter, down by about what the tree gained.
changes_only_when: you weigh the pot of soil yourself at the start and at the end and have to account for the difference
you are asked what got lighter when the tree got heavier, instead of what the tree needed to grow
you are shown that something you cannot see can sit on a balance and register a weight
misconceptions.slides_into: That the plant makes some of its own food but still takes the rest up out of the soil.

misconceptions.name: A tree's mass comes from the water it was given
misconceptions.belief: It is the water. You water a plant every day for years and all of that goes into it and stays there and builds it up.
misconceptions.predicts: A tree given twice as much water would end up about twice as heavy, so weighing the soil proves nothing.
changes_only_when: you are shown how little is left of a plant once it has been dried right out
you are asked whether the experiment you were just shown ruled water out, or only the soil
you are shown that something you cannot see can sit on a balance and register a weight
misconceptions.slides_into: That it was the water together with the minerals dissolved in it.

misconceptions.name: Growth is something the tree does, not stuff moving from somewhere
misconceptions.belief: The tree just grows. That's what trees do — it's alive, so it gets bigger, and the sun and the rain and the soil help it do that. The weight doesn't have to come from anywhere. Nothing else got smaller.
misconceptions.predicts: Nothing in the surroundings needs to lose any weight when the tree gains weight, so the question of what got lighter has no answer. Weighing the soil is not evidence about anything; it just shows again that plants need soil.
changes_only_when: you first agree, about some case you already believe, that when one thing gets heavier something else got lighter by the same amount
you are made to commit to what in the surroundings lost weight, and how much
you are walked through it question by question rather than shown one surprising demonstration
misconceptions.slides_into: That the stuff came up out of the soil after all.
